svg.title: The KV cliff: from 64 to 256 agentic sessions the KV pool fills and prefix hits collapse
svg.desc: A 40-cell KV pool (914,240 tokens, vLLM TP8, BF16 KV). At 64 sessions 15 of 40 cells are used (KV peak 0.37), prefix hit 88.4%, TTFT p90 1,214 ms, ITL p90 26.7 ms, all requests in SLO. At 256 sessions every cell fills, cached history is evicted and recomputed, requests queue (waiting p90 113), the hit falls to 52.0%, TTFT p90 rises to 17.9 s and ITL p90 to 216 ms; 0.05% of requests meet the SLO.
svg.text: The KV cliff: sessions outgrow the KV pool, hits collapse, work is redone
vLLM TP8, BF16 KV cache, agentic sessions (2,000-token shared prompt, +600 in / 200 out per turn)

g.text: KV in use 100% (256 sessions): new turns evict cached history
1. 64 sessions fit (KV peak 0.37). Each turn reuses its cached history: hit 88.4%.
2. 256 sessions need about 1.6M to 2.2M tokens of KV against a 0.91M pool: history is evicted and redone.
3. Result: hit 88% → 52%, TTFT p90 1,214 ms → 17.9 s, ITL p90 27 → 216 ms.
What moved it: an FP8 KV cache doubles the pool (TP8+EP8, 256 sessions: hit 89.0%, KV peak 0.70, 0 preemptions),
but TTFT p90 is still 4.10 s and ITL p90 56.4 ms there: only 18% of requests meet the SLO.

svg.text: Cells and queue are schematic; panel values are measured. 256-session run is count-capped (2,048 of 2,208 turns). Single runs.
Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 FP8 | 8x H100 SXM5 | Dynamo 1.6.0 + vLLM 0.31.0 | SLO: TTFT ≤ 2 s and ITL ≤ 50 ms per request
